problem: A chorus about the narrator's own loss keeps failing: every version explains what happened to him, and none of them sings.
technique: Move the camera off the narrator. Write the chorus as what he sees other people doing in the moment after the loss (on the walk home, in the car park), and give one line to naming a stranger as somebody's loved one. Keep the private loss in the verse, a one-line hinge, and the late sections.
example: Fender's first People Watching chorus summed up the town's debt and how tragedy had shaped him, and it sat unfinished for months. The chorus that worked came in LA, after he saw people sleeping rough on Hollywood Boulevard and remembered a grave marked 'Somebody's Sweetheart': strangers on treadmills and under billboards, someone's loved one on the street, and a narrator who can't stop running.
limits: One documented revision, generalised by the analyst; Fender does not say why the first chorus failed. Lexical comparison of tool-extracted transcript excerpts; no audio needed and none checked.
when_not: When the private detail is the point of the song (Kahan's Stick Season chorus is where his local facts live), or when no verse has yet set the stakes, so an outward chorus would read as detached social comment.
distinct_from: C43: says the chorus should tell the whole song; here it deliberately does not, and someone hearing only the chorus would not know anyone had died
C52: swaps an argument for named examples; this changes whose life the chorus is about
C23: keeps the addressee unnamed and anchors the feeling in an image; this is about the narrator's subject, not the addressee

problem: A grief or heartbreak song set as a slow ballad sinks: the setting matches the subject but not where the song ends up.
technique: Decide which stage of the feeling the lyric arrives at (acceptance, gratitude, hope) and set the tempo and feel to that stage; let the words carry the grief.
example: Asked whether a slower ballad would suit grief, Fender says he wanted the liberation of acceptance and something celebratory for a larger-than-life friend, so People Watching drives while its words move from loss to gratitude. He says he prefers yearning and hopeful writing to happy writing and admires ABBA's sad lyrics on uplifting music. Kahan says he wanted Stick Season heard as hopeful, because the season passes, and wanted to keep the casual, unserious energy of the phone demo.
limits: Tempo and feel are known from writer statements and press description only, not checked by listening.
when_not: If the lyric never reaches acceptance, an uplifting setting reads as denial or tone-deafness; some grief songs should stay in the room.
distinct_from: C07: lowers the verbal temperature of the verses (a lyric-register choice); this is the musical setting
C50: gets the last-chorus lift from texture; this sets the feel of the whole song
C21: non-lyric fixes for a weak chorus; this is a concept-level choice made before writing

problem: The writer fears a place-name or local detail in the chorus will shut out listeners who aren't from there.
technique: Keep the local facts in the chorus, but pair each one with an admission anyone could make (half the fault, waiting for friends, playing the victim), and put the portable image (a drive, a missed exit) in the verse.
example: Kahan says he feared the Vermont detail would alienate people and was surprised it connected. In Stick Season the chorus holds the state, the season's local name, the ex's mother and the Christmas homecoming, each beside a plain admission, while the verse carries the driving metaphor.
limits: The fear is documented; the pairing explanation is the analyst's, drawn from partial, tool-extracted transcript excerpts. Lexical; no audio needed. Kahan never says the pairing was deliberate.
when_not: When the local facts are scenery with no admission attached, the chorus becomes a postcard; for an artist with no tie to the place, it reads as borrowed.
distinct_from: C43: the opposite placement (verses private, chorus general); this is a documented counterexample and could be filed as a limit on C43 instead of a new card
C41: the place as a value system the narrator refuses; here the place is mood and season
C12: choose portable plainness or particular specificity; this keeps both by pairing them line by line
